name: P517 F6 fencing mutation probe (copy-out, r2): submodule non-fast-forward retry must reauthorize (run-git-sync.ts)
command: --test 'D=$(dirname {}); if [ -L "$D/run-git-sync.test.ts" ]; then cp --remove-destination <repo>/packages/operator-core/lib/harness/git-sync/run-git-sync.test.ts "$D/run-git-sync.test.ts" || exit 3; echo MATERIALIZED_TEST_COPY; fi; cd "${D%/lib/harness/git-sync}" && pwd && npx vitest run lib/harness/git-sync/run-git-sync.test.ts -t "F6: submodule non-fast-forward retry reauthorizes" --reporter=dot'
summary: Copy-out (default tier) mutation probe; the tracked tree was never mutated, so no file lock or git-sync lease was needed. The mutant lives only in the probe's repo mirror. The --test materializes a real copy of run-git-sync.test.ts beside the mirrored mutant, but only when the mirrored test is a symlink, so the real-tree baseline runs unchanged. Materializing the copy stops Vite from realpathing the symlinked test back into the real tree and importing the real module. Mutated control: 'F6: submodule non-fast-forward retry reauthorizes before another push'. The real-tree baseline passed 1 (159 skipped) and so did the unmutated-mirror baseline. The mutant swallows a beforePush (publication authority) refusal instead of refusing the push. That let the retry push proceed after the owner key became unavailable, and the test failed: expected 2 to be 1 (the push count). The probe reported MUTANT CAUGHT and verified run-git-sync.ts byte-identical afterwards. The unmutated mirror copy passed and the mutant failed on the push-count assertion, so the mutated module was the one loaded. This regenerates binding 16317, which went stale when run-git-sync.ts changed. The r1 probe (21:15-21:17Z, docs/evidence/p517-run-git-sync-f6-retry-reauth-mutation-copyout-2026-09-30-c8f54.json) measured blob af38742a, which a peer commit (12135961, EI-24712906810240170 post-stage guard) superseded before binding. This r2 probe measured the current committed bytes, which were clean and unchanged from before to after the probe.
